extracted.intended_audience: data producers, data re-users, archivists, and repository assessors
extracted.subtask_description: Operationalising the FAIR principles into an assessment tool (FAIRdat) to rate datasets on Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable criteria using a 5‑star scheme; intended for application to datasets across repositories. Focus is on producing independent, per-principle scores and an overall reusability score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findable (F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Findable – defined by a persistent identifier and detailed metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findability is assessed by the presence of a persistent identifier and sufficiently detailed metadata so that the dataset can be discovered. In FAIRdat this principle is one of three independently scored principles and is represented as a 5‑star criterion level. High findability contributes to overall reusability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible (A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accessible – well-defined license and access conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accessibility concerns clear licensing and access conditions that allow users to obtain or understand how to obtain the data. The page notes that accessibility elements have been placed under multiple FAIR principles in some presentations, and stresses defining accessibility so it can be scored independently. Accessibility receives a 1–5 star rating in the tool.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interoperable (I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interoperable – ready to be combined with other data by humans and machines: standardised formats and vocabulary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interoperability is judged by use of standardised formats, vocabularies and machine‑readable representations that enable combination with other data. The authors flag overlap in some presentations between interoperability and accessibility/reusability and require an operational definition that allows independent scoring. Interoperability is rated on the same 5‑star scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reusable (R) / FAIRness
rubrics_metrics.description: Reusable – ready to be reused in future research and processed using computational methods; in the FAIRdat implementation the original 'R' is calculated as an average of the scores for F, A and I to provide an overall 'FAIRness' or 'Reusability' score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tool treats R as the aggregate (mean) of Findable, Accessible and Interoperable star scores. The authors argue reuse criteria used in other implementations can often be accommodated under F, A or I, and that achieving high F/A/I typically increases reusability. The tool displays per‑principle star scores and the computed R score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent operationalisation of principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles must be defined so that each can be described and scored independently (no circular or cross‑listed criteria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors found ambiguity where terms (e.g., 'accessible') appeared under multiple principles, which prevents independent per‑principle scoring and can lead to 'messy' or misleading overall assessments. The tool therefore operationalises each principle with independent criteria so a dataset's score on one principle does not depend on another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five‑level star scoring per principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Each principle (F, A, I) is represented by five criterion levels corresponding to a 1–5 star rating in the FAIR profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FAIRdat tool uses a star/badge representation (influenced by Open Data Certificate and Tim Berners‑Lee’s 5‑star scheme). The project has outlined five criterion levels for Findable, Accessible and Interoperable, and maps assessment responses to these star levels. Stars are intended to be intuitive badges of dataset quality per principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment instrument design: limited question set with routing
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessments are run as a short survey (usually a maximum of 5 questions per principle) with routing logic to determine the star rating for each principle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pilot was implemented using SurveyMonkey; each principle typically has up to five questions and routing options that determine which questions are shown and how answers map to a star score. At the end of the assessment the tool displays the star score per principle and calculates the overall R score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness of catalogue and FAIR profile visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Associate a FAIR profile (per‑principle star scores and overall R) to each dataset in a FAIRdat database and/or at the dataset's repository location, and provide a catalogue of assessed datasets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The planned FAIRdat website would host documentation on scoring, a catalogue of datasets with FAIR profiles, and promote transparency and international adoption. Displaying profiles alongside datasets helps promote usage and reuse; implementation should provide guidance and essential documentation for scorers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of complementary assessment dimensions (legal, practical, technical, social)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of and where relevant include legal, practical, technical and social aspects of dataset quality as used in other badge schemes (e.g., Open Data Certificate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tool is influenced by existing badge schemes that evaluate datasets on dimensions beyond F/A/I, such as legal clarity, practical accessibility, technical standards and social/community factors. While FAIRdat focuses on F/A/I (and R as an aggregate), designers and assessors should consider these complementary dimensions when specifying question wording or interpreting scores.
